title: Shallow-Alignment KL Signature Replicated as a Cheap Open-Model Robustness Predictor

original_idea.body:
# Shallow-Alignment KL Signature Replicated as a Cheap Open-Model Robustness Predictor

**Problem:** The per-token aligned-vs-base KL signature has not been turned into a comparable scalar metric and correlated with attack robustness across open models.

**Direction:** Replicate the per-token KL measurement across ~6 open instruct models with base siblings, summarize each as a 'depth-of-alignment' scalar, then correlate with each model's measured prefilling/decoding ASR.

**Why it matters:** A one-pass KL signature predicting attack robustness gives small actors a cheap triage tool.

**Relevant context:** Qi et al. 2024 (arXiv:2406.05946).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: a cheap KL-based pre-attack robustness predictor is a defensible monitoring/triage tool, though robustness-as-safety has an indirect link.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Per-token KL on base/instruct pairs + correlation; guided but needs careful metric design across ~6 models.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused scalar-vs-ASR correlation; needs base/instruct pairs and ASR measurement, a few dependencies.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Cheap triage tool on public model pairs labs deprioritize; external-friendly.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference-only forward passes on base/instruct pairs, single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: KL visualization published; turning it into a predictive scalar across families may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: KL signature shown; predictive-metric framing plausibly open.
